cands.name: Natalie S. Murdock
cands.bio: North Carolina state senator for District 20 (Durham and Chatham), appointed by Gov. Roy Cooper on April 1, 2020. Former Durham Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor. Founded a communications consulting firm. Formerly deputy director of communications at the NC Department of Justice. UNC-Chapel Hill graduate.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace, where she grew up, or when she came to North Carolina. We found no documented position of hers on data centers or on development, and no stated positions on homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had. Her campaign site is apparently an older version from the 2022 race, and its platform page was cut off, so some current positions may be missing. The bills the site lists as sponsored were not checked against legislative records.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since April 2020 and re-elected four times. Elected Durham Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor in 2018. Founded a communications consulting firm in 2017. Previously deputy director of communications at the NC Department of Justice, and held roles at GoTriangle and in regional economic development.
qual.why: More than six years of legislative service plus local elected office and a business career put her in the high range for writing law and the state budget. Committee assignments were not counted.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign platform says she will work to increase state funding for programs that preserve and conserve water, and describes her work as a soil and water supervisor to reserve land, open spaces and drinking water.
